Revenue rose by about $27,710 per weekday, from the plan's total of roughly $10.57 million. The model reports it as a small net gain, and visits rose by only about 1,062 per weekday.

**Why it rose:** Pedestrianizing 2nd Street and charging $5 on I-80 shifted travel toward walking and transit. Walk minutes rose by about 63,374, and foot traffic rose on Mission (+19,656 per day), Beale (+16,716) and Market (+10,038). More people on foot means more stops at nearby shops.

**Winners:** Whole Cakes (+$1,811 per day), Reynoso Florist (+$1,791), Quality Shoe Repair (+$1,043), and the café Radiator (+$864).

**Losers:** Insomnia Cookies (−$945 per day), Golden Goose (−$818), and several cafés, including Blue Stone Lane (−$152), Philz (−$147) and Cafe Madeleine (−$128).

**Caveat:** The economic value of this gain depends on the assumed "retail net new share" parameter. Also, the model shows 42 people dropping out of commuting ("gone"), which is a cost of the charge.
